name: Banana Yellow
lede: Banana Yellow is the bright yellow of a banana skin, here as a vivid greenish yellow from the 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: The skin of the fruit
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary defines banana as the yellow of the banana skin and notes the variant *banana-yellow* [1]. The swatch comes from the xkcd survey of 2010 [2]. The nearest ISCC-NBS category is brilliant greenish yellow, about 6 units away [2]. Close neighbors are [[bright-yellow]], [[lemon-yellow]] and [[banana]] [3]. Their distances are 3.4, 3.6 and 4.6 units, so the plain Banana name is the farthest of the three, and the two yellows that carry no fruit name sit closer to this swatch than the fruit does [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 3 paintings in our archive of 23,781 hold this color, as photographed, rarer than 79% of named colors [4]. The earliest is a Gauguin of 1893 [4]. The word peaks in printed English in the 2010s, after rising fastest in the 2000s, though it also names the fruit [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, not pigment tests.
